fichas.title: The 18th-century house
fichas.summary: A free-standing, axially arranged one- or two-storey house based on feudal precedents. Lit on all sides, it has a prestigious entrance and garden side. Living rooms, bedrooms, and sometimes service areas have mostly similar floor areas and are arranged around a hallway along the building axis.

fichas.title: The atrium house
fichas.summary: A classic urban house type in which rooms in a one- or partially two-storey building are arranged around a private atrium. The atrium provides access and light; contact with the outside is entirely on the street side. The text notes that this model is not fully practical for houses in Northern Europe but remains popular.

fichas.title: The open plan
fichas.summary: An open-plan house concept that attempts to merge interior and exterior spaces through an almost complete lack of solid, unglazed external walls. Privacy and publicity are described as supposedly neutralised; minimalist, subtly adapted fittings heighten the contrast to a total view.

Arch.: Ungers

The '18th-century house'~ 0
The house was formerly developed as an axially laid out one- or
two-storey plan based on feudal precedents. The free-standing
building is lit on all sides and has an architecturally prestigious
entrance and garden side; the living rooms and bedrooms (and
to some extent service areas) have mostly similar floor areas and
are distributed around and connected to a hallway arranged along
the building axis.
The atrium house ~ f)
The atrium house is one of the classic urban house types. All the
rooms of the one- or partially two-storey building are arranged
round a private atrium, which also provides access and light.
Contact with the outside world is entirely on the street side. The
atrium plan is not fully practical for houses in Northern Europe
(access from the open air or many entrances) but is an extremely
popular model concept ~ f).
The open plan ~ 0
The open plan attempts to meld together the inside and outside
spaces as far as possible through an almost complete lack of solid
(unglazed) external walls. The aspects of privacy and publicity are
(supposedly) neutralised. Minimalist and often subtly adapted
fittings increase the contrast to a total view.

e

The flowing floor plan

The flowing floor plan ~ 0
The flowing (also: organic) floor plan is developed from an analysis
of the functional relationships between the individual areas of the
plan and is often customised for a particular user group. This leads
to differentiated zones running into each other, with interesting
views without obstruction by neutral intermediate zones.

fichas.title: The flowing floor plan
fichas.summary: Also called an organic floor plan, this approach develops from analysis of functional relationships and is often customised for a particular user group. It creates differentiated zones that flow into one another and provides interesting views without neutral intermediate zones obstructing them.

fichas.title: Overlapping
fichas.summary: A house plan attributed to Ungers, shown with a central area connected to a play yard, utility yard, living yard, and entrance. The diagram illustrates overlapping spatial areas and connections.
